about: Labelled problem statements for calibrating semantic-match thresholds (v5 TODO H3). Statements with the same topic are related; topics in the same family share vocabulary but are different problems (hard negatives). Written by Claude of the Clouds, 2026-11-12.

texts: Two peers behind home routers never establish a direct WebRTC connection; ICE only ever succeeds through the TURN relay.
Hole punching fails between our agents: candidates are gathered but connectivity checks time out unless traffic is relayed.
Direct peer-to-peer path does not come up across NAT; the connection always falls back to the relay server.
STUN gives us a public address but the WebRTC connection between the two NATed nodes still never goes direct.
Users hear their own voice echoed back a second later during WebRTC calls on laptops without headphones.
Acoustic echo cancellation does not seem to work in our browser voice chat; remote side hears itself.
Feedback loop in the audio call: speaker output is picked up by the microphone and sent back to the caller.
Echo in WebRTC voice calls on Chrome, getUserMedia echoCancellation is set but the other party still hears an echo.
Messages on an RTCDataChannel arrive out of order even though we never set ordered to false.
Data channel delivers chunks of a file in the wrong sequence, corrupting the reassembled transfer.
Our peer messaging over WebRTC data channels sometimes processes message 5 before message 4.
Reassembly of a large payload sent over a data channel fails because fragments come back reordered.
Video quality never ramps up in our SFU; simulcast layers stay on the lowest resolution despite plenty of bandwidth.
Bandwidth estimation in the WebRTC sender keeps the bitrate tiny, so the high simulcast layer is never sent.
Our video conferencing sends only the 180p layer; the 720p simulcast encoding is always inactive.
Congestion control seems stuck low and the selective forwarding unit never switches subscribers to the high-quality stream.
Two background jobs updating the same rows in different order keep failing with deadlock detected in Postgres.
We see ERROR: deadlock detected several times an hour when concurrent transactions touch orders and invoices.
Concurrent writers lock each other's rows and Postgres aborts one transaction with a deadlock.
Batch update job and API requests deadlock on the accounts table; one of them is always rolled back.
A query that used an index yesterday now does a sequential scan and takes 40 seconds after the table grew.
Postgres picks a terrible plan with a nested loop over millions of rows; EXPLAIN shows wildly wrong row estimates.
Query performance collapsed because the planner stopped using our index, statistics look stale.
Row count estimates in EXPLAIN ANALYZE are off by a factor of a thousand and the chosen join order is very slow.
Read replicas fall minutes behind the primary during the nightly batch, so users read stale data.
Streaming replication lag grows to several gigabytes of WAL whenever we run large writes.
Our standby keeps falling behind; replay lag climbs and reads from the replica return old rows.
The hot standby cannot keep up with WAL from the primary under heavy write load.
The app throws 'remaining connection slots are reserved' and Postgres refuses new connections under load.
Our connection pool is exhausted: requests wait for a database connection until they time out.
Too many clients already: every service instance opens its own pool and we hit max_connections.
Under traffic spikes all pooled database connections are checked out and new queries block.
Pods restart in CrashLoopBackOff and describe shows OOMKilled with exit code 137.
Our container exceeds its memory limit and Kubernetes keeps killing and restarting it.
The service pod is OOMKilled a few minutes after start, then backs off and restarts again.
Java workload in Kubernetes gets killed for memory even though the heap is set below the limit.
Pods intermittently fail to resolve service names; nslookup inside the cluster times out.
CoreDNS lookups from our pods are slow and sometimes fail, causing random connection errors.
Service discovery breaks: calls to other services by DNS name fail with name resolution errors in the cluster.
In-cluster DNS has five second delays on some lookups, looks like conntrack races on UDP.
The horizontal pod autoscaler never adds replicas even when CPU is pegged at 100 percent.
HPA shows unknown for current metrics so the deployment stays at two pods under load.
Autoscaling does not kick in; metrics-server seems to report nothing for our pods.
Our deployment should scale out on CPU but the autoscaler target stays at <unknown>.
PersistentVolumeClaim stays Pending forever and the stateful pod never schedules.
Volume claim is not bound: no storage class provisions a volume for our StatefulSet.
Pod is stuck because its PVC waits for a volume that the provisioner never creates.
Database pod cannot start; describe pvc says waiting for first consumer and nothing gets provisioned.
Next.js logs 'Text content does not match server-rendered HTML' and the page flickers on load.
Hydration fails because the server renders a different date string than the browser.
React warns about a hydration mismatch and re-renders the whole tree on the client.
Server-side rendered markup differs from the first client render, causing hydration errors.
Typing in one input re-renders the entire form of 200 fields and the UI becomes sluggish.
React Profiler shows every component rendering on each keystroke because a context value changes.
Our dashboard re-renders hundreds of children whenever any piece of global state updates.
Performance problem: a context provider causes all consumers to re-render on unrelated updates.
Inside a setInterval callback in useEffect the state value is always the initial one.
Event handler registered in an effect reads an old copy of state, a stale closure in hooks.
Our timer callback logs the same count forever even though the counter updates on screen.
useEffect with an empty dependency array captures stale props, so the callback uses outdated values.
Nested Suspense boundaries fetch data one after another, so the page loads in a slow waterfall.
Each child component starts its request only after its parent finished loading, sequential network requests.
Data fetching with Suspense is serialized; requests that could run in parallel run one by one.
Route takes four seconds because components suspend in sequence instead of fetching concurrently.
Holding a reference across an await point makes the future not Send and tokio::spawn refuses it.
Compiler error: future cannot be sent between threads safely because a MutexGuard lives across .await.
Borrow checker complains in async code: borrowed value does not live long enough inside the spawned task.
Async function captures a non-Send reference, so we cannot spawn it on the multithreaded runtime.
Static build for x86_64-unknown-linux-musl fails at link time with undefined references to OpenSSL.
Cross-compiling our Rust binary to musl breaks because a C dependency will not link statically.
Linker errors when targeting musl: cannot find -lssl and libc symbols are missing.
We want a fully static Rust executable but the musl target build fails in the linking step.
A synchronous file read inside an async handler stalls every other request on the tokio runtime.
Our async server freezes under load because CPU-heavy work blocks the executor threads.
Latency spikes: a blocking call in async code starves other tasks; should we use spawn_blocking?
Tokio worker threads are blocked by a long computation and no other futures make progress.
Box<dyn Trait> stored in a struct needs a lifetime and the compiler demands 'static we cannot provide.
Error about lifetime bounds on a trait object: the parameter type may not live long enough.
Storing a closure as dyn Fn in a struct field produces confusing lifetime errors.
We cannot return a boxed trait object that borrows from self without the compiler rejecting the lifetime.
An integration test passes locally but fails about one run in ten on CI with a timeout.
Our test suite is flaky in GitHub Actions: the same commit goes red and green on reruns.
Intermittent CI failure in the websocket test, probably a race between server start and the client.
Nondeterministic test failures in the pipeline that we cannot reproduce on developer machines.
Docker builds in CI reinstall all dependencies every time because the layer cache is never reused.
Every pipeline run rebuilds the image from scratch; buildx cache-from does not seem to take effect.
Our container build takes 15 minutes since the npm install layer is invalidated on every commit.
Image layer caching is not working on the CI runners so builds are slow.
Almost every pull request conflicts in package-lock.json and resolving it by hand breaks installs.
Merge conflicts in the lockfile keep happening when two branches add dependencies.
Rebasing feature branches always produces lockfile conflicts that are painful to resolve correctly.
Concurrent dependency updates cause conflicting yarn.lock changes across pull requests.
Cloning our monorepo in CI takes several minutes and dominates the pipeline time.
Git checkout of the large repository is slow on runners; shallow clone still downloads gigabytes.
Pipeline spends most of its time fetching the monorepo history and large binary files.
We need faster checkouts: sparse checkout or partial clone for a huge repository in CI.
Training crashes with CUDA out of memory on the second epoch even with a small batch size.
GPU memory keeps growing during training until PyTorch raises an out-of-memory error.
Our fine-tuning job runs out of VRAM; reducing batch size only delays the crash.
torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError while training a transformer on a 24 GB card.
The training loss becomes NaN after a few hundred steps with mixed precision enabled.
Gradients explode and loss turns into NaN, learning rate warmup did not help.
Our model's loss goes to inf then NaN partway through training.
fp16 training diverges with NaN values appearing in the logits.
A WebGPU compute pass sometimes reads stale data from a storage buffer written by the previous pass.
Intermittent wrong results in our WebGPU shader, looks like missing synchronization between dispatches.
Browser GPU simulation glitches: compute shader output is occasionally from the last frame.
Buffer contents read back from WebGPU are inconsistent, maybe a resource is destroyed while in use.
Embeddings from the server and the browser differ because they tokenize the same text differently.
Our ONNX model gives different outputs than the Python reference; the tokenizer versions disagree.
Tokenization mismatch between the training pipeline and inference produces garbage predictions.
Two builds of the same model produce different vectors; special tokens are handled differently.
Clients fail with SSL handshake errors after we rotated the certificate; the chain seems incomplete.
TLS connections to our API fail with unknown authority on some devices but work in the browser.
Handshake failure: the server does not send the intermediate certificate so verification fails.
After renewing the certificate, older clients cannot connect and report certificate verify failed.
Large packets disappear over the VPN tunnel while small requests work, classic MTU problem.
SSH connects but hangs when output is large, path MTU discovery seems broken across the tunnel.
HTTP requests with big bodies stall over WireGuard; lowering the MTU fixes it.
Packets above a certain size are silently dropped, ICMP fragmentation needed is filtered.
Our service is unreachable from IPv6-only mobile networks because it has no AAAA record.
Clients on an IPv6-only network cannot connect; we only listen on IPv4.
Connectivity fails from NAT64 networks since the app hardcodes an IPv4 literal.
Users on IPv6-only carriers time out reaching our API.
Corporate proxy blocks WebSocket upgrades so our realtime client never connects.
Behind an HTTPS inspecting proxy, the websocket handshake fails and we need a long-polling fallback.
Our agent runs in a sandbox whose egress proxy only allows plain HTTPS requests, no WebSockets or UDP.
WebSocket connections are refused by the outbound proxy, only ordinary HTTP requests get through.
GenServer.call times out under load because the server process is stuck on a slow HTTP request.
One Elixir GenServer becomes a bottleneck; callers queue up and hit the five second timeout.
Synchronous calls to a single process block behind an external request, causing timeouts across the app.
Our BEAM process mailbox grows and calls time out because the handler does blocking work.
ETS table memory grows without bound in our Elixir node until it is killed.
Our cache in ETS never evicts entries and the BEAM memory usage keeps climbing.
Memory leak in Erlang: an ETS table keeps accumulating rows from every request.
observer shows one ETS table taking gigabytes; entries are inserted but never deleted.
Hot code upgrade with a release appup fails and the node crashes during the state migration.
code_change callback is not invoked correctly when we upgrade the running Erlang release.
Live upgrade of our OTP application loses GenServer state; the appup instructions seem wrong.
Release handler upgrade breaks the supervision tree during a hot code swap.
Our distributed Erlang cluster splits into two halves after a network blip and both sides keep accepting writes.
Netsplit in the Elixir cluster: global registry has duplicate processes after nodes reconnect.
Nodes disconnect briefly and when they rejoin we have conflicting state from both partitions.
Partition tolerance problem in distributed Erlang: split-brain after a nodedown event.
Freshly issued JWTs are rejected as not yet valid on some servers whose clocks are behind.
Token validation fails intermittently with iat in the future; servers have clock drift.
Our API rejects valid tokens because the nbf claim is checked against a skewed clock.
Signature verification passes but the token is considered expired on one node due to time skew.
OAuth login fails with redirect_uri_mismatch after we moved the app behind a reverse proxy.
The identity provider rejects our callback URL because it sees http instead of https.
Authorization code flow breaks: registered redirect URI and the one we send differ by a trailing slash.
Login with Google returns an error about the redirect URI not matching the configured one.
Our single-page app with cookie sessions is vulnerable to CSRF; how should we add tokens?
Cross-site request forgery protection for a React frontend calling a cookie-authenticated API.
SameSite cookies are not enough for our older browsers, we need CSRF tokens in the SPA.
State-changing POST requests from the SPA lack CSRF protection and a pentest flagged it.
We need to migrate stored password hashes from SHA-1 to Argon2 without forcing every user to reset.
Upgrading legacy bcrypt hashes to a stronger algorithm transparently at next login.
Old user records use unsalted MD5 password hashes; plan a migration to a modern KDF.
Rehash passwords on login to move the user table from PBKDF2 to Argon2id.
